newsitem.title: CANADA: Bloc's Duceppe praises separatist effort in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Bloc's Duceppe praises separatist effort in Quebec.

text.p: Bloc Quebecois leader Gilles Duceppe praised his separatist supporters on Monday night for helping the party win a majority of the 75 Quebec seats in Canada's federal election.
Results showed the Bloc winning 45 Quebec seats, down from the 54 it won in the 1993 election, but better than public opinion polls showed leading up to the vote.

But the Bloc was ousted as the official opposition in Canada's parliament by Western Canada-based Reform, which took a tough line on Quebec's secessionist aspirations and accused other Canadian political parties of trying to appease Quebec.
Speaking to a boisterous crowd of supporters at a nightclub, Duceppe said it was an eventful night because of the close battles in many Quebec districts.
He pointedly referred to the tight race in the Saint-Maurice district, which Canadian Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien won by about 1,200 votes over an old rival, the Bloc's Yves Duhaime.
"We have worked in a convinced and determined fashion because we all have the same objective, to give ourselves a sovereign country," Duceppe said.
Duceppe said the election campaign showed that it was impossible to reconcile the constitutional aspirations of Quebec with those of the rest of Canada.
"There is only one way to get out of the Canadian constitutional quagmire, and that is the sovereignty of Quebec," Duceppe declared.

He said the "hard line" taken toward Quebec during the campaign by Chretien, which he said was magnified "like never before" by right-wing Reform Party leader Preston Manning, was proof of the wide gulf between Quebec and the rest of Canada.
Speaking in English, Duceppe said none of the plans put forward by the other parties would prevent Quebec voters from choosing what they want -- whether to remain in Canada or form a new country.
Duceppe added in English that Quebec sovereignty would be the best solution for both Quebec and the rest of Canada.
